_comment: Proposed content for game/data/conversations.json, in the format design/dialogue.md decides. Ordered nodes, first match wins, top to bottom — so the most specific lines come first and the file reads in the order it will fire. The last node of every conversation must be unconditional. Rules being held: name a creature by its tell and never by its type; every NPC has a relationship with attention; no templating, ever — every line is written whole. A party_has condition can only ever fire for a creature that has stats, so it may not name a roster creature that is not yet statted — that is dialogue written for content which does not exist.

conversations.about: Her kiln has been cold since spring. She is the one who still notices, and has not decided whether that is a virtue.

nodes.say: Oh, you've brought the one that won't admit it's cold. Look at it — sat as near the dead kiln as it can get, telling itself the morning's only just started. Nobody's going to correct it. I'm certainly not.
You've got one of the new collars on. No — it's fine. Everyone does. My brother does.
Whatever you've got there came off warm ground, I can tell from here. They all stand like that. Like they're about to be needed.
You keep coming back to a cold yard. That's either very stupid or the first sensible thing I've seen this year.
Kiln's been cold since spring. Something still wakes up when I light the small one, though. Comes and sits where the heat would be, if there were any.

conversations.about: He took the shortcut, cheerfully, and would recommend it. narrative.md's antagonist is a method rather than a person, and this is what the method looks like when it is being kind to you.

nodes.say: There, see? No fuss. You'll wonder what the standing about was ever for.
Offer stands. Take one. I'll not think less of you either way — I'd think less of me, standing out here in the cold on principle.
No. That's rather the point of it, isn't it. Saves everyone a morning.
You're doing it the long way. I did, once. Stood out here half a day waiting for a thing to make its mind up about me.
Now I've got a collar and a full yard and my afternoons back. You should have one.

conversations.about: She has measured this pass for eleven years. She could once name everything on it. She cannot now, and she has not connected the two facts.

nodes.say: That one won't come down for you, you know. Not properly. They stand about looking like they've somewhere better to be, and they never do go.
Back again. You'll have noticed it's quieter up here than the maps suggest. Everyone says weather. It isn't weather.
Mind the edge. It doesn't care that you're careful.
Eleven years I've measured this pass. Used to be I could put a name to everything that crossed it. Can't now — my eyes, probably. You get to an age.
